property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets baseToken to the _baseToken argument passed in; the mutant sets baseToken always to address(0), so there exists inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken and thus the mutant will violate the rule.

For any inputs to initialize, the correct contract sets baseToken equal to the provided _baseToken parameter (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize returns); the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken causing the property to fail.

For any initialize(...) inputs, the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the provided _baseToken argument (i.e., c.baseToken() == _baseToken); the mutant that assigns baseToken = _nft breaks this by making c.baseToken() != _baseToken for some inputs.

For any caller and input arguments, after initialize(...) completes on the correct contract the public nft() equals the _nft parameter passed (the contract stores the provided NFT address); the mutant which assigns nft = msg.sender violates this because nft() will instead equal the caller for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed to initialize (reference holds for all inputs); the mutant sets nft to address(0) and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed pool's public nft() equals the _nft parameter passed to initialize (reference satisfies this); the mutant sets nft to the factory address so nft() != _nft for some inputs, breaking the rule.

For any input parameters to initialize, the stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument provided (i.e. c.changeFee() == _changeFee) in the reference; the mutant increments the stored value by 1 so this equality will fail for some fuzzed _changeFee values.
For any initialize(...) call the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed; the mutant that forces changeFee to 0 breaks this when _changeFee != 0.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed to initialize; the mutant assigns changeFee from _feeRate instead, so for inputs where _changeFee != _feeRate the mutant will differ.

For any inputs to initialize within admissible bounds, the reference contract preserves the provided _feeRate in its public feeRate getter (feeRate() == _feeRate); the mutant forces feeRate to 0 so this equality can be violated for some fuzzed _feeRate != 0.

For any admissible _feeRate (<=5000) passed to initialize, the stored feeRate equals the input _feeRate (reference preserves exact assignment); the mutant that assigns feeRate = _feeRate + 1 will cause stored feeRate != _feeRate for some fuzzed _feeRate (e.g., any value ≤5000).

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored feeRate after initialize must equal the _feeRate argument passed; the mutant that swaps assigning feeRate and changeFee can cause feeRate to be stored incorrectly for some inputs and thus violate this property.

After initialize(...) returns successfully, the stored feeRate equals the _feeRate parameter passed; the mutant that swaps assigning feeRate and changeFee can cause feeRate to be stored incorrectly for certain fuzzed inputs (due to overlapping storage/packing interactions), so the property will fail on the mutant for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, after a successful call the contract's public feeRate must equal the _feeRate argument; swapping the order of assigning feeRate and changeFee in the mutant can corrupt the stored feeRate for some packed-storage inputs, so the mutant will violate this rule for some fuzzed inputs.

For all inputs, after initialize(...) returns successfully the public feeRate must equal the _feeRate argument passed; the mutant that swaps the order of assigning feeRate and changeFee can corrupt feeRate due to storage packing for some fuzzed (_feeRate, _changeFee) pairs and thus violate this rule.
